# Style Guide

This document outlines the coding standards and best practices for contributing to Discourse Graphs.

## TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## UI Guidelines

- Use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use Tailwind classes.
- Use platform-native UI components first ([blueprintjs for Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/5BB8h4I7b), [Lucide icons for Obsidian](https://help.obsidian.md/Contributing+to+Obsidian/Style+guide), etc), with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

## Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

## Code comments

Ask: **What would a maintainer get wrong if this comment were removed?** If there is no specific answer, remove it.

Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.

Before keeping a comment, check:

- **Necessary:** Would removing it hide information needed to safely change or use the code?
- **Accurate:** Does it match what the code actually does, including relevant limitations and exceptions?
- **Concise:** Can it be shortened without losing necessary information?
- **Durable:** Will it still matter after this PR merges?
- **Local:** Is it next to the code that depends on the information?

Prefer one or two short sentences. Use longer explanations or examples when the constraint requires them; this is not a hard length limit.

Do not restate function names, types, test names, assertions, or obvious operations. Do not repeat an explanation already documented at its source; link to it when needed.

Put implementation history, review iterations, scope justifications, and ticket splits in inline GitHub comments. Keep durable constraints and known limitations in code or linked documentation. Link to the decision when describing behavior as agreed or accepted.

Agents must check added and modified comments against these criteria before handoff. Authors must review them manually before requesting review.

## Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Co-locate code with its primary usage. Export it only for a concrete reuse need.
- Move code to `/utils` when it is shared across multiple call sites. Consider a shared package only after the code has stabilized and proven broadly reusable.
- Ground code movement in a current use case. Moving code because it feels cleaner adds churn without a clear functional benefit.
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly:

```typescript
// ❌ Unclear and inline
const result = items.filter(
  (x) => x.date > now && x.status === "active" && !x.isArchived,
);

// ✅ Clear and reusable
const getActiveUnarchivedItems = (items: Item[]) => {
  return items.filter(isActiveAndUnarchived);
};

const isActiveAndUnarchived = (item: Item) => {
  return item.date > now && item.status === "active" && !item.isArchived;
};
```

- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary:

```typescript
  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
  // Check if user can access premium features
  const check = (user: User) => { ... }

  // ✅ Self-documenting function name
  const hasValidPremiumSubscription = (user: User) => { ... }
```

- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions:

```typescript
// ❌ Large, multi-purpose function
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  // 30 lines of validation
  // 20 lines of transformation
  // 15 lines of formatting
};

// ✅ Composed of focused functions
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  const validatedData = validateDataFormat(data);
  const transformedData = transformToDesiredFormat(validatedData);
  return formatForDisplay(transformedData);
};
```

## Documentation

- Use sentence case by default in docs and UI copy. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or page titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.

## Code hygiene

- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
- Handle errors gracefully and log enough context to diagnose failures without exposing credentials or sensitive data.

## Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.
You are working on the public-facing website for Discourse Graph.

## Dependencies
Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Documentation Style
Use sentence case for documentation copy by default. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

   - Nothing in `apps` or `packages` calls it. Roam and Obsidian create accounts through `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_accounts_in_space`, which are `SECURITY DEFINER`. `GET` and `DELETE` in `[id].ts` are unaffected.
   - If the route stays, undo the validator edit (it is cosmetic) and say in the PR that the route is dead on purpose.
2. Change the grant comment in the migration and in `supabase/schemas/account.sql` from "until it is added here" to "until it is added to these grants". In the migration, "here" points at the wrong place.

Branch `eng-2447-stop-clients-from-claiming-platform-accounts-or-adding`, cut from `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally` (8b805889c). Local only; nothing committed as of October 30, 2026. Ticket: https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2447/stop-clients-from-claiming-platform-accounts-or-adding-accounts-to

## Open decisions before the PR

1. The Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account` (`apps/website/app/api/supabase/platform-account/route.ts`) can no longer succeed. Decide whether to delete `route.ts` (recommended) or keep it and say it is dead on purpose.
   - Its `getOrCreateEntity` upsert is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` on every payload column. Postgres needs `UPDATE` rights on every column in that `SET` list, even without a conflict, and `platform` and `account_local_id` are no longer granted. Every call fails with `42501`.
   - A plain insert would fail too: a new account has no `LocalAccess` row, so the insert policy's only way through was `dg_account = auth.uid()`, which the grant now closes.
   - Nothing in `apps` or `packages` calls it. Roam and Obsidian create accounts through `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_accounts_in_space`, which are `SECURITY DEFINER`. `GET` and `DELETE` in `[id].ts` are unaffected.
   - If the route stays, undo the validator edit (it is cosmetic) and say in the PR that the route is dead on purpose.
2. Change the grant comment in the migration and in `supabase/schemas/account.sql` from "until it is added here" to "until it is added to these grants". In the migration, "here" points at the wrong place.
3. Post a scope comment on ENG-2447: the `INSERT` grant also leaves out `id`, the validator also drops `write_permission` (both agreed with the ticket author on October 30), and the route removal if chosen.

## Known merge conflict

ENG-2443 and this branch both add a `const untyped` helper to `features/step-definitions/stepdefs.ts`, with different parameter types. Whichever merges second gets a duplicate declaration; keep one, typed on the logged-in client.

## Evidence (October 30, 2026, uncommitted working tree)

- Before the fix, `features/accountWriteAccess.feature` failed on the claim rows (`dg_account`, `agent_type`, `platform`, `account_local_id`, insert of an owned account) and on the `LocalAccess` inserts into s3. Moves and deletes were already refused through the API: the select policy hides the rows from a filtered write, and `safeupdate` (preloaded for `authenticator`) rejects an unfiltered one. In SQL, an unfiltered `DELETE FROM "LocalAccess"` as s2's login removed rows of s3 (rolled back).
- After the fix: the feature passes 5 of 5; full cucumber suite 39 scenarios, 439 steps, after `supabase db reset` (CLI 2.122.0, image 17.11.0.006).
- `pnpm ci:validate` passed. sqruff clean on the migration. Lint shows only warnings that were there before.
- Delegated full review: one Low finding, the dead route above. Confirmed unaffected: Obsidian `updateUsername` (writes only `name`), website reads, the definer account functions, the edge functions (service role). Schema and migration match.

## Draft PR body

Title: `ENG-2447 Stop clients from claiming platform accounts or adding accounts to spaces they don't edit`

```markdown
## Reviewer brief

- Result: clients can no longer set who owns a platform account, change what identifies it, or add an account to a space they don't edit.
- Review focus: the `PlatformAccount` column grants in `packages/database/supabase/migrations/20261030160000_restrict_account_writes.sql`. A new column is not client-writable until it is added to them.
- Risk or follow-up: before applying in production, look for accounts with a `dg_account` that are not `anonymous`, and for `LocalAccess` rows whose account has no other tie to that space's editors.

## Verification

- `features/accountWriteAccess.feature`: the claim rows and the `LocalAccess` inserts failed before the change and pass after it. The move and delete scenarios already passed before: through the API, the select policy hides those rows and `safeupdate` rejects an unfiltered write.
- Full cucumber suite: 39 scenarios, 439 steps, all passing after `supabase db reset`.
- `pnpm ci:validate` passed.

## Loom video

<!-- Paste the Loom link. -->

## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-2447 and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: the `PlatformAccount` `INSERT` grant also leaves out `id`; the Website validator also drops `write_permission`.
- Required now: `write_permission` is no longer insertable, so the route would fail on it anyway; leaving out `id` keeps clients from choosing ids in the shared sequence.
- Anyone affected or consulted: Yes, the ticket author.
- Decision: ENG-2447 comment (to post).

## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.

## Local delegated full review

- [x] Ran a comprehensive review of the entire final diff in a subagent with a fresh context. Use `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
```

content.text:
I checked the review's finding in psql and it holds. The `POST /api/supabase/platform-account` route can no longer succeed.

I ran both writes on the test database as a space login (`authenticated`), in a transaction I rolled back:

- **The route's upsert,** with no existing row to conflict with: it fails with `permission denied for table PlatformAccount`. Postgres needs `UPDATE` rights on every column in the `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` list before it runs.
- **A plain insert of a new unowned account:** it fails the insert policy (`new row violates row-level security policy`).

So the route doesn't break anything that used to work. Before this change it could only create an account owned by the caller, which is exactly the claim the ticket removes, and nothing in `apps` or `packages` calls it.

I saved the PR body, the review finding, the evidence and this check to `packages/database/eng-2447-pr-notes.md`. The file is untracked.

The three decisions are listed there and still waiting on you:

1. Delete `route.ts` (my recommendation), or keep it and say it's dead on purpose.
2. Change the grant comment's wording to "added to these grants".
3. Post the scope comment on ENG-2447.

input.body:
Implementation finding: the Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account` route is deleted instead of having `dg_account` removed from its validator.

* After the column grants, the route can never succeed. Its `getOrCreateEntity` upsert is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` on every column it sends, and Postgres requires `UPDATE` on each of them even when there is no conflict. `platform` and `account_local_id` are no longer granted, so every call fails with `permission denied for table PlatformAccount`.
* A plain insert fails too: a new account has no `LocalAccess` row, so the insert policy's only way through was `dg_account = auth.uid()`, which the grants close.
* Before this change the route could only create an account owned by the caller, which is the claim this ticket removes. Nothing in `apps` or `packages` calls it; Roam and Obsidian create accounts through `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_accounts_in_space`.
* Both failures were verified in `psql` on the local test database as a space login, in a rolled-back transaction. Found by the delegated review; agreed with the ticket author on October 30.

{"id":"ENG-2447","uuid":"00edd5f6-778a-486b-a714-e7ef715c8128","title":"Stop clients from claiming platform accounts or adding accounts to spaces they don't edit","description":"## Problem

* Any client with editor access to a space can claim the space's unowned platform accounts, including the space's anonymous account. The `PlatformAccount` write policies let it set `dg_account` to its own user, and then it owns the account: it can update and delete it.
* Any client can tie an account to a space it has no access to. The `LocalAccess` write policies check the account, never the row's `space_id`. An editor of a space can add that space's unowned accounts to any other space, and an account owner can add their own account to any space.
* Both should be fixed before the account policies are rewritten in <issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account">ENG-2446</issue>, so its scenarios assert the fixed behavior. Once `LocalAccess` carries claims in the DG accounts work, a forged row would become a way to act for a space.

## Solution

* Replace the table-wide `INSERT` and `UPDATE` grants on `PlatformAccount` for `authenticated` with column grants:
  * `INSERT` leaves out `id`, `dg_account` and `write_permission`.
  * `UPDATE` covers only `name`, `active` and `metadata`. It leaves out `dg_account`, `agent_type`, `platform`, `account_local_id` and `write_permission`.
* Add `space_id = any((SELECT public.my_space_ids('editor'))::bigint [])` to the `LocalAccess` insert, update and delete policies, keeping their account condition.
* Remove `dg_account` from the validator of the Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account`.

## Done When

* Scenarios show that a client logged in as a space's anonymous account cannot set `dg_account` on an unowned account, by insert or update, and cannot change `agent_type`, `platform` or `account_local_id`. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that a client cannot add a `LocalAccess` row for a space where it lacks editor access, whether it edits the account's space or owns the account. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that such a client also cannot move a `LocalAccess` row into that space or delete one from it. These already pass before the change: through the API, the select policy hides those rows from a filtered write, and `safeupdate` rejects an unfiltered one. The space check is added to the update and delete policies anyway, so they don't depend on either.
* Scenarios show that what must keep working still works: space creation, `upsert_account_in_space` for an editor, an account owner renaming their account, and an editor renaming an unowned author account of their space.

## Out of Scope

* A claim function or claim table. Nothing sets `dg_account` as `authenticated` today; the DG accounts spec decides the claim mechanism.
* Dropping the unused `write_permission` column.
* Adding one's own account to another space. That waits for claim infrastructure, gated on an attested `LocalAccess` row.
* Checking that a `LocalAccess` row's account and space share a platform. After this change, someone who edits spaces on two platforms can still tie an unowned account of one to the other by a direct insert. No client writes `LocalAccess` directly.
* Rewriting the account policies to run once per query (<issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account">ENG-2446</issue>).

## Notes

* Decisions and evidence: Roam [vtxvgZEKp](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vtxvgZEKp>) (claiming) and [wB_q939-M](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/wB_q939-M>) (`LocalAccess` space check), each with a "Decided October 30" block.
* Space creation and group creation write as `service_role`, and `upsert_account_in_space` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and never sets `dg_account`, so the grants don't affect them.
* Blocks <issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account">ENG-2446</issue>. Related to <issue id="1a223b96-4ee6-4f9f-ac40-ebc67c45c2a0" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2439/require-editor-access-to-a-space-before-adding-accounts-to-it">ENG-2439</issue>, which also tightens `upsert_account_in_space`. Keep the branch local and cut from `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally`, like the other security fixes.
* Before applying in production, look for claims and forged rows: accounts with a `dg_account` that are not `anonymous` (only space accounts should have one), and `LocalAccess` rows whose account has no other tie to that space's editors.

Both are done in Linear.

- **Ticket description:** the Solution now says `INSERT` leaves out `id`, `dg_account` and `write_permission`.
- **Comment:** I took "account.sql" to mean the platform-account route, since that's the implementation finding. If you meant something else, tell me. - **Ticket text I left alone:** the Solution bullet "Remove `dg_account` from the validator" stays, because the comment covers the change and expansions get a note rather than an edit.
- **Notes file:** the draft PR body's Scope check in `packages/database/eng-2447-pr-notes.md` now lists only the route deletion and points at that comment.

For the grant comment, in both the migration and `account.sql`, I'd write:

```sql
-- Clients cannot set who owns an account (dg_account) or change what identifies it (agent_type, platform, account_local_id).
-- Inserts and updates are granted per column: a new column is not client-writable until it is added to these grants.
-- A PostgREST upsert needs UPDATE on every column it sends, so clients cannot upsert accounts; they go through upsert_account_in_space.
```

- **The first line** names the protected columns, so a reader doesn't have to work them out from the grant lists.
- **The second line** is the maintenance trap. It names the grants rather than saying "here".
- **The third line** is the constraint that made the route impossible, and the next person writing a client upsert would hit it.

content.text:
{"id":"ENG-2447","uuid":"00edd5f6-778a-486b-a714-e7ef715c8128","title":"Stop clients from claiming platform accounts or adding accounts to spaces they don't edit","description":"## Problem

* Any client with editor access to a space can claim the space's unowned platform accounts, including the space's anonymous account. The `PlatformAccount` write policies let it set `dg_account` to its own user, and then it owns the account: it can update and delete it.
* Any client can tie an account to a space it has no access to. The `LocalAccess` write policies check the account, never the row's `space_id`. An editor of a space can add that space's unowned accounts to any other space, and an account owner can add their own account to any space.
* Both should be fixed before the account policies are rewritten in <issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account">ENG-2446</issue>, so its scenarios assert the fixed behavior. Once `LocalAccess` carries claims in the DG accounts work, a forged row would become a way to act for a space.

## Solution

* Replace the table-wide `INSERT` and `UPDATE` grants on `PlatformAccount` for `authenticated` with column grants:
  * `INSERT` leaves out `id`, `dg_account` and `write_permission`.
  * `UPDATE` covers only `name`, `active` and `metadata`. It leaves out `dg_account`, `agent_type`, `platform`, `account_local_id` and `write_permission`.
* Add `space_id = any((SELECT public.my_space_ids('editor'))::bigint [])` to the `LocalAccess` insert, update and delete policies, keeping their account condition.
* Remove `dg_account` from the validator of the Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account`.

## Done When

* Scenarios show that a client logged in as a space's anonymous account cannot set `dg_account` on an unowned account, by insert or update, and cannot change `agent_type`, `platform` or `account_local_id`. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that a client cannot add a `LocalAccess` row for a space where it lacks editor access, whether it edits the account's space or owns the account. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that such a client also cannot move a `LocalAccess` row into that space or delete one from it. These already pass before the change: through the API, the select policy hides those rows from a filtered write, and `safeupdate` rejects an unfiltered one. The space check is added to the update and delete policies anyway, so they don't depend on either.
* Scenarios show that what must keep working still works: space creation, `upsert_account_in_space` for an editor, an account owner renaming their account, and an editor renaming an unowned author account of their space.

## Out of Scope

* A claim function or claim table. Nothing sets `dg_account` as `authenticated` today; the DG accounts spec decides the claim mechanism.
* Dropping the unused `write_permission` column.
* Adding one's own account to another space. That waits for claim infrastructure, gated on an attested `LocalAccess` row.
* Checking that a `LocalAccess` row's account and space share a platform. After this change, someone who edits spaces on two platforms can still tie an unowned account of one to the other by a direct insert. No client writes `LocalAccess` directly.
* Rewriting the account policies to run once per query (<issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account">ENG-2446</issue>).

## Notes

* Decisions and evidence: Roam [vtxvgZEKp](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vtxvgZEKp>) (claiming) and [wB_q939-M](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/wB_q939-M>) (`LocalAccess` space check), each with a "Decided October 30" block.
* Space creation and group creation write as `service_role`, and `upsert_account_in_space` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and never sets `dg_account`, so the grants don't affect them.
* Blocks [ENG-2446](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account>). Related to [ENG-2439](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2439/require-editor-access-to-a-space-before-adding-accounts-to-it>), which also tightens `upsert_account_in_space`. {"id":"ENG-2447","uuid":"00edd5f6-778a-486b-a714-e7ef715c8128","title":"Stop clients from claiming platform accounts or adding accounts to spaces they don't edit","description":"## Problem

* Any client with editor access to a space can claim the space's unowned platform accounts, including the space's anonymous account. The `PlatformAccount` write policies let it set `dg_account` to its own user, and then it owns the account: it can update and delete it.
* Any client can tie an account to a space it has no access to. The `LocalAccess` write policies check the account, never the row's `space_id`. An editor of a space can add that space's unowned accounts to any other space, and an account owner can add their own account to any space.
* Both should be fixed before the account policies are rewritten in <issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account">ENG-2446</issue>, so its scenarios assert the fixed behavior. Once `LocalAccess` carries claims in the DG accounts work, a forged row would become a way to act for a space.

## Solution

* Replace the table-wide `INSERT` and `UPDATE` grants on `PlatformAccount` for `authenticated` with column grants:
  * `INSERT` leaves out `id`, `dg_account` and `write_permission`.
  * `UPDATE` covers only `name`, `active` and `metadata`. It leaves out `dg_account`, `agent_type`, `platform`, `account_local_id` and `write_permission`.
* Add `space_id = any((SELECT public.my_space_ids('editor'))::bigint [])` to the `LocalAccess` insert, update and delete policies, keeping their account condition.
* Remove `dg_account` from the validator of the Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account`.

## Done When

* Scenarios show that a client logged in as a space's anonymous account cannot set `dg_account` on an unowned account, by insert or update, and cannot change `agent_type`, `platform` or `account_local_id`. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that a client cannot add a `LocalAccess` row for a space where it lacks editor access, whether it edits the account's space or owns the account. They fail before the change and pass after it.
* Scenarios show that such a client also cannot move a `LocalAccess` row into that space or delete one from it. These already pass before the change: through the API, the select policy hides those rows from a filtered write, and `safeupdate` rejects an unfiltered one. The space check is added to the update and delete policies anyway, so they don't depend on either.
* Scenarios show that what must keep working still works: space creation, `upsert_account_in_space` for an editor, an account owner renaming their account, and an editor renaming an unowned author account of their space.

## Out of Scope

* A claim function or claim table. Nothing sets `dg_account` as `authenticated` today; the DG accounts spec decides the claim mechanism.
* Dropping the unused `write_permission` column.
* Adding one's own account to another space. That waits for claim infrastructure, gated on an attested `LocalAccess` row.
* Checking that a `LocalAccess` row's account and space share a platform. After this change, someone who edits spaces on two platforms can still tie an unowned account of one to the other by a direct insert. No client writes `LocalAccess` directly.
* Rewriting the account policies to run once per query (<issue id="c2814438-ab26-4232-81f1-54c69dfa8cba" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account">ENG-2446</issue>).

## Notes

* Decisions and evidence: Roam [vtxvgZEKp](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vtxvgZEKp>) (claiming) and [wB_q939-M](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/wB_q939-M>) (`LocalAccess` space check), each with a "Decided October 30" block.
* Space creation and group creation write as `service_role`, and `upsert_account_in_space` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and never sets `dg_account`, so the grants don't affect them.
* Blocks [ENG-2446](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2446/check-account-table-access-once-per-query-and-drop-the-per-row-account>). Related to [ENG-2439](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2439/require-editor-access-to-a-space-before-adding-accounts-to-it>), which also tightens `upsert_account_in_space`. Keep the branch local. It is stacked on <issue id="c187a719-3f2e-45e5-9088-1d61d65601e8" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2443/check-rls-access-once-per-query-instead-of-once-per-row">ENG-2443</issue>: it revokes no function `EXECUTE`, so it does not need the upgraded stack from `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally`.
* Before applying in production, look for claims and forged rows: accounts with a `dg_account` that are not `anonymous` (only space accounts should have one), and `LocalAccess` rows whose account has no other tie to that space's editors.

input.content:
Feature: Account table access
  User story:
  * As a user of a plugin
  * Logged in through a given space's anonymous account
  * I want to see and keep up to date the accounts of the spaces I share
  * And nobody else should see or change them without access to those spaces

  Acceptance criteria:
  * Partial access to a space shows its accounts, reader access also shows their identifiers and the space's account list
  * Editors of a space can write the identifiers of its unowned accounts, and delete those accounts
  * An account's owner can write its identifiers and delete it
  * Access tokens are visible and writable by their owner; unowned tokens are visible to everyone

  Background:
    Given the database is blank
    And the user user1 opens the Roam plugin in space s1
    And the user user2 opens the Roam plugin in space s2
    And the user user3 opens the Roam plugin in space s3
    And user of space s1 creates group g1
    And user of space s1 adds space s2 to group g1
    And the account of space s1 is called anon1
    And the account of space s2 is called anon2
    And access_token are added to the database:
      | request_id | access_token | code |
      | t-none     | secret-none  | c    |

content.text:
The ENG-2446 scenarios are written but haven't run yet. The run wipes the test database, so it needs your OK.

**What's new:**

- **`features/accountTableAccess.feature`**, nine scenarios on the current policies:
  - Visibility, from s2's login: with no shared access, with `partial` on s1, and with `reader` on s1. It covers `PlatformAccount`, `AgentIdentifier`, `LocalAccess` and `access_token`.
  - Visibility for a client that isn't logged in, on `access_token` only. `anon` has no grant on the other tables.
  - `AgentIdentifier` writes by an editor and by a reader.
  - `PlatformAccount` deletes by an editor and by a reader.
  - `access_token` writes by s2's login.
- **`stepdefs.ts`**:
  - One step for visible rows per account table, plus a variant for a client that isn't logged in.
  - Write steps for identifiers and for access tokens.
  - A `delete` operation on the account write step. It isn't undone, because a delete cascades, so deletes go last in their tables.
- Typecheck and Prettier are clean. Lint shows only the three warnings that were already there.

**Two things I left out on purpose, both on `access_token`:**

- The policy is `FOR ALL USING (platform_account_id IS NULL OR is_my_account(...))`. That means any logged-in client can update or delete an unowned token. Asserting that as "allowed" in a branch that will become public would document a weakness. It belongs to the open `access_token` question on ENG-2436, so the scenarios only show that unowned tokens are visible to everyone and can be inserted.
- I didn't test inserts by a client that isn't logged in.

**Expectations to check.** I wrote the visibility rows from reading the policies. A row that disagrees with today's behavior gets looked at before I change it, so the scenarios keep recording what the policies do now, not what I assumed. In particular:

- `partial` shows an account but not its identifiers. The `AgentIdentifier` select policy uses `account_in_shared_space` at its default level, `reader`.
- `LocalAccess` rows need `reader`.

**The run:** check that `docker ps` shows `supabase_db_test`, then run `features/accountTableAccess.feature` and `features/accountWriteAccess.feature` on the database you've just reset. Shall I?

The ENG-2446 scenarios pass on the current policies. The two account features have 14 scenarios between them, and the full suite passes: 69 scenarios, 760 steps. Typecheck and Prettier are clean. Nothing is committed.

**Every visibility row matched what I read from the policies:**
- `partial` on s1 shows its accounts, but not their identifiers or its `LocalAccess` rows.
- `reader` shows all three.
- A client that isn't logged in sees only the unowned token.

**Three adjustments:**
1. **"The database is blank" now also clears `access_token`.** When an account is deleted, its tokens stay as unowned rows, so the seed rows collided with the next scenario's.
2. **Some accounts can't be deleted at all.** The foreign key from `AgentIdentifier` to `PlatformAccount` has no `ON DELETE` action. So no client can delete an account that has identifiers, even when the policy allows it, as for an editor deleting an unowned author account.
   - The delete scenarios now use author accounts without identifiers (`author1` in s1, `author3` in s3), so the policy is what decides. A comment in the feature says why.
   - Whether identifiers should cascade is a question for later, not for this ticket.
3. **A denial I replaced.** Deleting `user3` would have been refused by that same foreign key, so it didn't test the policy. `author3` replaces it.

**Still left out on purpose:** writes by any logged-in client to unowned access tokens, which belong with ENG-2436's open `access_token` question.

**Next:**
- Add the two helpers, `my_platform_account_ids()` and `account_ids_in_shared_spaces(level)`, with explicit grants. `anon` needs one too, because the `access_token` policy calls `is_my_account` on behalf of clients that aren't logged in.
- Rewrite the policies and the `PlatformAccount` branch of `generic_entity_access`.
- Drop the three functions.
- Regenerate `dbTypes`.
- Record `EXPLAIN` timings before and after.

Shall I go on?

Title: Drop the unused access_token table

## Problem

* The `access_token` table is unused: no app, package or edge function reads or writes it. The `access_token` names in the Roam and Obsidian admin panels and in the Website's `auth/token` route are Supabase session tokens, not this table.
* Its policies are still live. `anon` can read and insert rows, and any logged-in client can update or delete a row that has no `platform_account_id`.
* Its policy is also the only reason `is_my_account` must stay callable by `anon`, and it would have to be rewritten in ENG-2446 with the other account policies.

## Solution

* Add a migration that drops `public.access_token`.
* Remove `supabase/schemas/access_token.sql` and its entry in `schema_paths` in `supabase/config.toml`.
* Regenerate `dbTypes.ts`.

## Done When

* After the migration, `public.access_token` no longer exists, and no schema file, config entry or generated type refers to it.
* The full cucumber suite passes.

## Out of Scope

* Dropping `is_my_account`. ENG-2446 drops it with the other per-row account functions.
* Other Supabase advisor findings (ENG-2436).

## Notes

* Agreed with Michael Gartner that the table is unused and can be deleted.
* Before applying in production, check the table's row count and latest `created_date`, to confirm nothing writes it.
* Blocks ENG-2446, so its account scenarios and helpers don't need to cover the table. Related to ENG-2436.
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Start ENG-2446 (account-table RLS once per query, drop the per-row account functions). Before that, take the design decisions for the security candidates vtxvgZEKp (claiming unowned accounts) and wB_q939-M (`LocalAccess` space check), and implement them as ENG-2447.
   - ENG-2447 is implemented, committed by the user, and rebased onto ENG-2443. Its PR is delayed because it is a security fix. Its PR body and notes are in `packages/database/eng-2447-pr-notes.md`.
   - ENG-2446 scenarios are written and green on the current policies.
   - Latest user message:
     - The `access_token` table is unused and agreed with Michael for deletion; a Linear issue is needed, possibly as a prior step to ENG-2446 to simplify it.
     - AgentIdentifier should cascade on account delete, but that's another scope.
     - Identifiers might belong on `auth.users` later, but they stay on PlatformAccount for now.
     - "In all cases, they should stay unreadable cross-space until we have a policy for controlled disclosure."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Postgres column privileges:
     - `REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE` on the table, then `GRANT INSERT (cols)` and `GRANT UPDATE (cols)`.
     - `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` needs UPDATE on every column in the SET list, even with no conflict.
   - RLS behavior:
     - A filtered UPDATE or DELETE also applies the SELECT policy.
     - An UPDATE without WITH CHECK applies USING to the new row.
     - `safeupdate` is preloaded for `authenticator`, so PostgREST rejects an unfiltered update or delete.
   - Definer views bypass RLS; invoker views need grants on the base table.
   - SECURITY DEFINER functions:
     - `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space`, `create_account_in_space`.
     - The platform is taken from the Space row, so accounts link only within one platform.
   - The edge functions `create-space` and `create-group` write as `service_role` (secret key).
   - The AgentIdentifier→PlatformAccount FK has no ON DELETE action, so no client can delete an account that has identifiers.

Title: Drop the unused access_token table

## Problem

* The `access_token` table is unused: no app, package or edge function reads or writes it. The `access_token` names in the Roam and Obsidian admin panels and in the Website's `auth/token` route are Supabase session tokens, not this table.
* Its policies are still live. `anon` can read and insert rows, and any logged-in client can update or delete a row that has no `platform_account_id`.
* Its policy is also the only reason `is_my_account` must stay callable by `anon`, and it would have to be rewritten in ENG-2446 with the other account policies.

## Solution

* Add a migration that drops `public.access_token`.
* Remove `supabase/schemas/access_token.sql` and its entry in `schema_paths` in `supabase/config.toml`.
* Regenerate `dbTypes.ts`.

## Done When

* After the migration, `public.access_token` no longer exists, and no schema file, config entry or generated type refers to it.
* The full cucumber suite passes.

## Out of Scope

* Dropping `is_my_account`. ENG-2446 drops it with the other per-row account functions.
* Other Supabase advisor findings (ENG-2436).

## Notes

* Agreed with Michael Gartner that the table is unused and can be deleted.
* Before applying in production, check the table's row count and latest `created_date`, to confirm nothing writes it.
* Blocks ENG-2446, so its account scenarios and helpers don't need to cover the table. Related to ENG-2436.
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

Feature: Account table access
  User story:
  * As a user of a plugin
  * Logged in through a given space's anonymous account
  * I want to see and keep up to date the accounts of the spaces I share
  * And nobody else should see or change them without access to those spaces

  Acceptance criteria:
  * Partial access to a space shows its accounts
  * Reader access also shows their identifiers and the space's account list
  * Editors of a space can write the identifiers of its unowned accounts, and delete those accounts
  * An account's owner can write its identifiers and delete it
  * Access tokens are visible and writable by their owner; unowned tokens are visible to everyone

  Background:
    Given the database is blank
    And the user user1 opens the Roam plugin in space s1
    And the user user2 opens the Roam plugin in space s2
    And the user user3 opens the Roam plugin in space s3
    And user of space s1 creates group g1
    And user of space s1 adds space s2 to group g1
    And the account of space s1 is called anon1
    And the account of space s2 is called anon2
    And access_token are added to the database:
      | request_id | access_token | code |
      | t-none     | secret-none  | c    |
    And access_token are added to the database:
      | request_id | access_token | code | _platform_account_id |
      | t-anon2    | secret-anon2 | c    | anon2                |
      | t-user1    | secret-user1 | c    | user1                |

  Scenario: Without shared access, a space sees only its own account rows
    Then a user logged in space s2 should see these account table rows:
      | table           | rows            |
      | PlatformAccount | anon2, user2    |
      | AgentIdentifier | user2           |
      | LocalAccess     | user2@s2        |
      | access_token    | t-anon2, t-none |

  Scenario: Partial access shows a space's accounts, not their identifiers
    When SpaceAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_uid | _space_id | permissions |
      | g1           | s1        | partial     |
    Then a user logged in space s2 should see these account table rows:
      | table           | rows                |
      | PlatformAccount | anon2, user1, user2 |
      | AgentIdentifier | user2               |
      | LocalAccess     | user2@s2            |
      | access_token    | t-anon2, t-none     |

  Scenario: Reader access also shows identifiers and the space's account list
    When SpaceAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_uid | _space_id | permissions |
      | g1           | s1        | reader      |
    Then a user logged in space s2 should see these account table rows:
      | table           | rows                |
      | PlatformAccount | anon2, user1, user2 |
      | AgentIdentifier | user1, user2        |
      | LocalAccess     | user1@s1, user2@s2  |
      | access_token    | t-anon2, t-none     |

  Scenario: A client that is not logged in sees only unowned tokens
    Then a client that is not logged in should see these account table rows:
      | table        | rows   |
      | access_token | t-none |

  Scenario: Editors write the identifiers of their spaces' unowned accounts
    When SpaceAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_uid | _space_id | permissions |
      | g1           | s1        | editor      |
    Then a user logged in space s2 should get these identifier write results:
      | operation | account | result  |
      | insert    | user1   | allowed |
      | update    | user1   | allowed |
      | delete    | user1   | allowed |
      | insert    | user2   | allowed |
      | insert    | anon2   | allowed |
      | insert    | user3   | denied  |
      | update    | user3   | denied  |
      | delete    | user3   | denied  |

  Scenario: Readers cannot write identifiers
    When SpaceAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_uid | _space_id | permissions |
      | g1           | s1        | reader      |
    Then a user logged in space s2 should get these identifier write results:
      | operation | account | result |
      | insert    | user1   | denied |
      | update    | user1   | denied |
      | delete    | user1   | denied |

  # An account with identifiers cannot be deleted by any client: the AgentIdentifier foreign key
  # has no ON DELETE action. These accounts have none, so the policy decides.
  Scenario: Editors delete their spaces' unowned accounts, and owners their own
    When SpaceAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_uid | _space_id | permissions |
      | g1           | s1        | editor      |
    And PlatformAccount are added to the database:
      | $id     | name    | platform | account_local_id |
      | author1 | author1 | Roam     | author1          |

Feature: Account write access
  User story:
  * As a user of a plugin
  * Logged in through a given space's anonymous account
  * I want to keep the accounts of my space's authors up to date
  * But nobody should claim an account, or tie it to a space, through a plugin login

  Acceptance criteria:
  * A plugin login cannot set the owner of an account, or change what identifies it
  * Account names stay editable by editors of the account's space and by the account's owner
  * A space's account list can only be written by editors of that space

  Background:
    Given the database is blank
    And the user user1 opens the Roam plugin in space s1
    And the user user2 opens the Roam plugin in space s2
    And the user user3 opens the Roam plugin in space s3
    And user of space s1 creates group g1
    And user of space s1 adds space s2 to group g1
    And SpaceAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_uid | _space_id | permissions |
      | g1           | s1        | editor      |
    And the account of space s2 is called anon2

  Scenario: An editor cannot claim an account or change what identifies it
    Then a user logged in space s2 should get these account write results:
      | operation | account | column           | value     | result |
      | update    | user1   | dg_account       | own login | denied |
      | update    | user1   | agent_type       | anonymous | denied |
      | update    | user1   | platform         | Obsidian  | denied |
      | update    | user1   | account_local_id | changed   | denied |
      | insert    | user4   | dg_account       | own login | denied |

  Scenario: Account names stay editable
    Then a user logged in space s2 should get these account write results:
      | operation | account | column | value   | result  |
      | update    | user1   | name   | renamed | allowed |
      | update    | user2   | name   | renamed | allowed |
      | update    | anon2   | name   | renamed | allowed |
      | update    | user3   | name   | renamed | denied  |

  Scenario: An editor can still add accounts to a space through the account functions
    When user user2 upserts these accounts to space s1:
      """json
      [{ "account_local_id": "user4", "name": "user4" }]
      """
    Then a user logged in space s1 should see 3 PlatformAccount in the database

  Scenario: Only editors of a space can add an account to it or move one into it
    Then a user logged in space s2 should get these space membership write results:
      | operation | account | space | new space | result  |
      | insert    | user1   | s3    |           | denied  |
      | insert    | anon2   | s3    |           | denied  |
      | update    | user1   | s1    | s3        | denied  |
      | insert    | user1   | s2    |           | allowed |
      | insert    | anon2   | s1    |           | allowed |
      | delete    | user1   | s1    |           | allowed |

  # Through the API these deletes were refused even before the delete policy checked the space:
  # a filter makes the select policy hide the rows, and safeupdate rejects a delete without one.
  Scenario: Only editors of a space can remove an account from it
    Given LocalAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_id | _space_id |
      | user1       | s3        |
      | anon2       | s3        |
    Then a user logged in space s2 should get these space membership write results:
      | operation         | account | space | new space | result |
      | delete            | user1   | s3    |           | denied |
      | delete            | anon2   | s3    |           | denied |
      | unfiltered delete | user1   | s3    |           | denied |
      | unfiltered delete | anon2   | s3    |           | denied |

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/maparent/OpenSource/discourse-graph/.claude/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.

skills.content:

# DG Delegated Full Review

Use this skill only when the user invokes it directly or an explicitly requested workflow invokes it. Do not select it automatically.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. Look for it in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

Run the review outside the primary agent's context. Do not modify files, fix findings, or delegate from the review subagent.

## Workflow reference

May be selected by `$*-run-scoped-engineering-workflow` at step 6 through its review dispatcher. Standalone use remains supported. This skill owns the single review subagent; never route back through the personal dispatcher. Preserve any caller-supplied acceptance boundary alongside the review target.

## Resolve the target

- Preserve a pull request, branch, commit, diff, or other review target supplied by the user.
- Otherwise, review all staged, unstaged, and untracked changes in the current working directory.
- If the working tree is clean, review the current branch against its merge base with the configured upstream or default base branch.

## Run the review

Create exactly one read-only subagent or task in the current working directory. Use the host-specific path that matches the available tools without asking the user which host is running:

- In Codex, spawn a subagent (not a new user-visible task) and direct it to run `/review` for the resolved target.
- In Claude Code, use an `Agent` subagent and direct it to run `/review`, the alias for `/code-review`. Use `/code-review` if the alias is unavailable.
- In another agent host, use its task or subagent mechanism and give the worker the natural-language review instructions below.

If the worker cannot invoke the slash command, have that same worker follow these instructions instead. Do not start a replacement worker or perform the review in the primary context.

```text
Perform a read-only, defect-first review of the requested code changes. Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code and tests to verify each issue. Report only concrete, actionable regressions introduced by the change. List findings by severity with precise file and line references. If there are no qualifying findings, return "No findings." Do not modify files or delegate the review.
```

Wait for the worker to finish. Return its findings to the primary conversation, preserving priorities and file references. If the worker fails, report the failure instead of completing the review inline.

## Close the review task

Capture the result before cleanup.

- In Codex, close the completed subagent when a non-destructive close or archive action is available. Otherwise report that the runtime does not support cleanup.
- Claude Code subagents are ephemeral and need no separate archive action.
- In another host, close or archive the completed task when a non-destructive lifecycle action is available.

Do not permanently delete a transcript or worktree as a substitute for closing or archiving it.

skills.name: scope-check
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/maparent/OpenSource/discourse-graph/.claude/skills/scope-check

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- understand-anything:architecture-analyzer: Analyzes a codebase's file structure, summaries, and import relationships to identify
logical architectural layers and assign every file to exactly one layer. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:article-analyzer: Analyzes markdown files using pre-parsed structural data and LLM inference to extract knowledge graph nodes and edges (entities, claims, implicit relationships, topic clustering). (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:assemble-reviewer: Reviews the output of merge-batch-graphs.py for semantic issues the script
cannot catch. Recovers dropped nodes/edges and fills cross-batch gaps. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:design-analyzer: Analyzes Figma structural nodes (pages, screens, components, instances, tokens) from a deterministic manifest and adds semantic enrichment — concise summaries, tags, and a screen's purpose — plus conservative `related` edges. Does NOT invent structural nodes or edges. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:domain-analyzer: Analyzes codebases to extract business domain knowledge — domains, business flows, and process steps. Produces a domain-graph.json that maps how business logic flows through the code. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:file-analyzer: Analyzes batches of source files to produce knowledge graph nodes and edges.
Extracts file structure, functions, classes, and relationships using a two-phase
approach: structural extraction script followed by LLM semantic analysis. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:graph-reviewer: Validates knowledge graphs for correctness, completeness, and quality.
Runs systematic checks and renders approval or rejection decisions. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:knowledge-graph-guide: Use this agent when users need help understanding, querying, or working
with an Understand-Anything knowledge graph. Guides users through graph
structure, node/edge relationships, layer architecture, tours, and
dashboard usage. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:project-scanner: Scans a codebase directory to produce a structured inventory of all project files,
detected languages, frameworks, import maps, and estimated complexity. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:tour-builder: Designs guided learning tours through codebases, creating 5-15 pedagogical steps
that teach project architecture and key concepts in logical order. (Tools: All tools)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- create-obsidian-release: Create a release for the Discourse Graphs Obsidian plugin from a requested semantic version. Use when asked to create or prepare an Obsidian plugin release.
- dg-assess-security-advisories: Assess Discourse Graphs Dependabot alerts for actual exposure, produce evidence-backed reports, and carry out approved dismissal or remediation decisions. Use for individual advisories or review batches.
- dg-create-engineering-ticket: Create concise Discourse Graphs Engineering tickets in Linear with the canonical template, correct readiness status, an active existing project (none for unprojected Obsidian work), and existing labels (including `Obsidian plugin` for Obsidian work). Use when the user asks to create or draft an Engineering ticket; do not use for Feedback tickets.
- dg-create-roam-render-html-code: Wrap a completed HTML artifact in a Roam-compatible React iframe renderer and save it as a local code file. Use when the user asks to turn HTML output into Roam render HTML code.
- dg-delegated-full-review: Run a comprehensive, read-only code review in a separate subagent, return the findings to the primary agent, and close or archive the review task when supported. Use only when explicitly invoked for a pull request, branch, commit, diff, or current changes.
- dg-engineering-writing-style: Draft and revise engineering emails, chat messages, requests, follow-ups, status updates, engineering tickets, PR comments, issue reports, release notes, technical documentation, and other team writing in the shared Discourse Graphs style. Use whenever a Discourse Graphs engineer asks to write, rewrite, phrase, shorten, clarify, or polish team communication or documentation, unless they request a different style.
- dg-pr-adherence-check: Review a PR or local diff for adherence to Discourse Graphs code standards and PR requirements, report concerns to the author, and return a Standards check checkbox. Use before handoff or requesting review, alongside scope-check.
- dg-roam-load-extension: Build, register, activate, and verify the local Discourse Graphs Roam extension, then run an optional feature test in the same Playwright context. Use for live apps/roam proof on Windows or macOS without repeating browser, login, and folder-loading setup.
- dg-roam-playwright-session: Open one authenticated Roam Research Playwright context with a Discourse Graphs test slot on Windows or macOS. Use when testing apps/roam, capturing proof, inspecting live Roam behavior, or reusing the same page and profile across several checks.
- next-best-practices: Next.js best practices - file conventions, RSC boundaries, data patterns, async APIs, metadata, error handling, route handlers, image/font optimization, bundling.
- openspec-apply-change: Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change. Use when the user wants to start implementing, continue implementation, or work through tasks. Also use when the user says "openspec apply", "opsx apply", or "openspec implement".
- openspec-archive-change: Archive a completed OpenSpec change in the experimental workflow. Use when the user wants to finalize and archive a change after implementation is complete. Also use when the user says "openspec archive" or "opsx archive".
- openspec-explore: Enter OpenSpec explore mode - a thinking partner for exploring ideas, investigating problems, and clarifying requirements in a project that uses OpenSpec. Use when the user wants to think through something before or during an OpenSpec change. Also use when the user says "openspec explore" or "opsx explore".
- openspec-propose: Propose a new OpenSpec change with all artifacts generated in one step. Use when the user wants to quickly describe what they want to build and get a complete proposal with design, specs, and tasks ready for implementation. Also use when the user says "openspec propose" or "opsx propose".
- openspec-sync-specs: Sync delta specs from an OpenSpec change to main specs. Use when the user wants to update main specs with changes from a delta spec, without archiving the change. Also use when the user says "openspec sync" or "opsx sync".
- openspec-update-change: Update an OpenSpec change by revising its existing planning artifacts and keeping them coherent with one another. Use when the user wants to revise a change's plan, fold new decisions into it, or reconcile its artifacts after an edit. Also use when the user says "openspec update change" or "opsx update". If the user means the openspec update CLI command, which refreshes generated files, run that command instead. Never edits code.
- react-best-practices: React best-practices reviewer for TSX files. Triggers after editing multiple TSX components to run a condensed quality checklist covering component structure, hooks usage, accessibility, performance, and TypeScript patterns.
- roam-global-tailwind: Use Roam Research's globally loaded Tailwind CSS safely in RoamJS extensions. Trigger when Codex writes, reviews, or refactors Roam extension UI that relies on Roam's global Tailwind utility classes; checks whether utilities, responsive or state variants, arbitrary syntax, newer Tailwind names, colors, or important modifiers are available; or decides whether styling must instead live in extension-owned CSS or a separately compiled Tailwind bundle.
- scope-check: Compare a pull request or Git diff with a Linear engineering ticket's Done When criteria and produce a copy-ready PR scope check. Use when preparing or reviewing a PR, checking whether an implementation introduced broader abstractions or unsupported cases, or documenting why added scope is required now.
- shadcn: shadcn/ui expert guidance — CLI, component installation, composition patterns, custom registries, theming, Tailwind CSS integration, and high-quality interface design. Use when initializing shadcn, adding components, composing product UI, building custom registries, configuring themes, or troubleshooting component issues.
- turborepo: Turborepo monorepo build system guidance.
